text:
incident-bot: PAGER: high 5xx rate detected on prod edge (ingress path /v1/generate). 5m error-rate 14.8% > threshold 5%. Paging oncall: @jamie-oncall

jamie-oncall: taking pager. looking

sanjay: I can join, saw traces showing lots of upstream 503s hitting text-generator pool

jamie-oncall: checking envoy stats now

emily-sre: fyi I saw a config roll ~1h ago: route weight shuffle + new retry policy present. could be related

jamie-oncall: curling envoy admin ->
```bash
curl -s http://envoy-admin.prod:9901/stats | egrep "upstream_rq_5xx|cluster.text-gen" | tail -n 20
upstream_rq_5xx: 4123
cluster.text-gen.upstream_rq_5xx: 4108
cluster.text-gen.upstream_rq_503: 3890
cluster.text-gen.upstream_rq_retry: 8200
```

sanjay: upstream_rq_retry > upstream_rq_5xx — looks like retries are firing repeatedly (amplification)

maria-eng-runtime: I pulled the config change: `routes/v1-generate.yaml` now has `retry_on: 5xx,gateway-error` and `num_retries: 3` and there are no circuit_breakers set for cluster.text-gen

emily-sre: that combo is dangerous on bursty backends. a single overloaded host + retries -> fanout -> more overload

jamie-oncall: rolling hypothesis: recent weight flip pushed traffic to a partially unhealthy subset; LB retry policy amplified failures and saturated upstreams

ops-lead: @jamie-oncall prioritize mitigation: disable retries on the route or set `num_retries: 0`, and add a short-term circuit-breaker. low blast radius first

jamie-oncall: agreed. doing hotfix:
- patch route to `num_retries: 0` (remove retry_on flags)
- set `per_try_timeout` to 150ms
- add circuit_breakers on cluster.text-gen: `max_connections: 5000`, `max_pending_requests: 200`
- apply via configmap rollout to prod envoys

deploy-bot: infra-deploy triggered: lb-config v2026-03-15-hotfix-1 by jamie-oncall

maria-eng-runtime: applying patch now ->
```bash
kubectl -n infra apply -f routes/v1-generate-hotfix.yaml && kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/envoy
```

jamie-oncall: watching metrics and traces (watching 1m windows)

(30s later)

jamie-oncall: envoy stats after hotfix ->
```bash
# after apply (snapshot)
upstream_rq_5xx: 4237 -> 4280 (brief spike)
cluster.text-gen.upstream_rq_5xx: 4216 -> 22
cluster.text-gen.upstream_rq_503: 4001 -> 18
cluster.text-gen.upstream_rq_retry: 8325 -> 28
error-rate overall: 14.8% -> 1.5%
```

emily-sre: great. add :thumbsup: to thread. I'll update runbook to note default safe values for retries and require cb when retries enabled

ops-lead: Customer-impact check: CS reported elevated errors for heavy-concurrency customers. CS notified orgs: org-231, org-809, org-17 (message template sent)

maria-eng-runtime: capturing diffs for postmortem: `git diff routes/v1-generate.yaml HEAD~1` + deploy audit logs

jamie-oncall: followups assigned: emily-sre -> runbook + PR for safer defaults; sanjay -> grafana panels for retry amplification; maria-eng-runtime -> verify canary + add test that simulates intermittent 503s with retries enabled

ops-lead: escalate to a postmortem if we confirm config change bypassed review. please ping me with timeline

deploy-bot: lb-config v2026-03-15-hotfix-1 rolled out to 3 edge clusters (nodes: edge-eu-1, edge-us-3, edge-ap-2)

jamie-oncall: monitoring for 15m, will handoff to emily-sre at +30m

emily-sre: taking 30m watch now. added myself to the incident rotation note. starting postmortem doc draft -> https://pm.internal/incidents/6161616161

jamie-oncall: TL;DR: misconfigured route retries (num_retries=3 + retry_on=5xx) combined with a weight swap to an unhealthy subset caused retry amplification -> upstream exhaustion -> high 5xx. Mitigation: disabled retries + added cb + per-try-timeout. Error-rate returned to normal. Will author RFC for safer default LB settings

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> Severity: S2. Mitigated at 6161616190. Postmortem owner: emily-sre

emily-sre: I'll schedule a 1-hour post-incident review tomorrow. notes will include playbook changes and an automatic pre-deploy check to prevent enabling retries without cb limits.

jamie-oncall: thanks team — nice fast mitigation. :white_check_mark:
